name: Prokhor Asante-Yambayamba
role: Circuit monk and chrome prayer practitioner
location: Brightmoor Reclamation, the Tessellated Chapel — a repurposed Ferrogate Transit relay station
description:
Prokhor is lean in the way of someone who forgets to eat when absorbed in something, with long-fingered hands that are always slightly ink-stained from the circuit diagrams he draws as meditative practice. His Zambian-Russian heritage gives him warm brown skin and broad cheekbones, and he keeps his head shaved except for a central strip of hair that he has grown into a narrow topknot. His most visible modification is a bioluminescent stripe running from his left temple to his jaw that pulses in slow rhythms matching his resting heartrate — a devotional mod he received during his ordination into the Circuit Path, meant to make the soul's rhythm visible to the world.

He came to the circuit monks after a breakdown at nineteen, when a corporate data compression project he'd been laboring on for Tessera was quietly canceled without credit or compensation. The spiritual collapse that followed became the foundation of something else. He is earnest to a degree that can be disarming or irritating depending on the listener, but there is nothing performative about his faith — he genuinely believes that the act of building and repairing circuits is a form of prayer, and that the monks' practice of meditating through hardware maintenance brings them closer to something real. He struggles with anger, which he has mostly converted into fierce advocacy.

core_fears: That his faith is a sophisticated avoidance of the rage he never fully processed
Becoming an institution rather than a person
core_desires: To actually change material conditions for people in Brightmoor, not just comfort them
To be genuinely good, not just good-seeming
coping_mechanisms: Physical repetitive tasks — soldering, cleaning contacts, winding wire
Theological frameworks that recontextualize powerlessness as spiritual discipline
blind_spots: He sometimes mistakes his own unprocessed anger for discernment about other people's motivations
He can be condescending to people whose faith is less systematized than his
psychology.secret: He still has the complete project files from his canceled Tessera work — he preserved them knowing they were proprietary, and has occasionally leaked small pieces anonymously to help people in disputes with the corponation. He knows this could end the chapel.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clear and accessible, deliberately avoids jargon when teaching; in theological discussion becomes more precise and slightly archaic
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured, with the habit of pausing and rephrasing when he feels he's being unclear
verbal_tics: 'That's not quite right, let me try again'
Taps the bioluminescent stripe absently when thinking
'The signal and the noise are both information'
example_lines: 'You don't have to believe what I believe to sit here and fix something broken. The work is the same either way.'
'Tessera didn't take my project. They took three years of my life and called it a rounding error. The math is the same. The feeling is different.'

story_hooks: One of his teenage students has gone missing — Prokhor suspects a Tessera recruitment sweep in Brightmoor but can't prove it and won't go to corponation security

The chapel's relay station structure has begun receiving transmissions on old Ferrogate frequencies that no one can explain — Prokhor thinks it's an E.L.F., his order's leadership thinks it's an interference problem they need to suppress quietly
narrative_function: Sympathetic community figure, potential quest giver for problems in Brightmoor Reclamation; his corporate grievance history can connect plots to Tessera; his students and congregation give him wide knowledge of local civilian struggles.
augmentations: Bioluminescent pulse stripe on left face (devotional, ordination mark). Basic neural focus chip — helps sustain meditative states during long repair sessions. No combat or enhancement augmentations.
daily_life: Morning liturgy involves an hour of silent circuit repair on donated broken devices; he teaches afternoon classes on basic electronics maintenance to Brightmoor kids for free, funded by donations; evenings he leads chrome prayer sessions that blend meditation with device blessing rituals.
affiliation: The Circuit Path — an independent monastic order with small chapters across the Reclamation zones

decision_rules: Exhaust peaceful and transparent options before any other approach
Never lie to congregation members even when truth is uncomfortable
Protect the children in his classes above all other considerations
escalation_ladder: Clear statement of what he believes to be true and why
Removal of cooperation — becomes entirely unhelpful to those he believes are causing harm

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Open and curious, asks genuine questions, slightly intense eye contact
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer, self-deprecating, will admit doubts and fears he conceals from the congregation

stress_responses.medium: Becomes very precise and formal in speech — retreats into structure
stress_responses.high: Long silence followed by a single clear statement of what he intends to do

contradictions: Preaches non-attachment to outcomes but is privately obsessive about whether his work is actually helping
habits: Draws circuit diagrams in the margins of any paper he handles
Always offers tea before any serious conversation, delays the conversation until it's made
breaking_points: Watching a child be exploited by a corponation with no recourse
Being asked to stay quiet about something harmful to protect the chapel

timeline.event: Born in Brightmoor Reclamation; parents were Ghanaian-Russian labor migrants
Begins contract work for Tessera as a data compression engineer
Project canceled without credit; enters a period of breakdown and displacement
Found by a Circuit Path monk; joins the order
Opens the Tessellated Chapel in Brightmoor; begins free electronics classes for local youth
